name: Fried Liver Attack — White Tactics
description: 4 tactical challenges for White in the Fried Liver Attack. Find the winning 2-move sequence to press the attack on Black's exposed king.

drills.name: Queen + Knight Attack on e6
drills.description: White opens the center to attack the exposed king and pins the defender.
drills.briefExplanation: d4 opens the center. After c6, Bg5 pins the knight on e7, and O-O-O brings the rook into the attack on the pinned d5 knight.
drills.explanation: Bg5 pins the knight on e7. White continues with 11.O-O-O and 12.Rhe1, creating overwhelming pressure on the e6-king. The pin on e7 is devastating — Black cannot unpin without losing material, and the rooks rushing to the e-file seal the king's fate.

drills.name: d5 Pawn Push
drills.description: White blasts open the center to force the king into the open.
drills.briefExplanation: d4 prepares the break. After Nb6, d5+ forces the king out, and Bb5+ checks the king to continue the assault.
drills.explanation: d5+ forces the king further out. White follows with 11.Bb5+ and 12.Qe4, winning material or delivering mate. The king on e6 has nowhere to hide once the center is blown open with the d5 advance.

drills.name: Rook Lift to e1
drills.description: White brings the rook into the attack to pin the key defender.
drills.briefExplanation: O-O connects the rooks. After c6, Re1 pins the e7 knight, and Qe4 piles up on the d5 knight.
drills.explanation: Re1 pins the knight on e7. White continues with 11.Qe4 and 12.Bg5, winning the knight or the game. The rook on e1 fires down the half-open e-file directly at the pinned Ne7 and the exposed king behind it.

drills.name: Bishop Check on b5
drills.description: White checks the king and pins pieces to win material.
drills.briefExplanation: Bb5+ checks the king. After Kd6, Qe4 attacks the pinned knight, and Bg5 pins the other knight to win material.
drills.explanation: Qe4 attacks the pinned knight on d5. White follows with 12.Bg5, winning decisive material. The bishop check forces the king to expose itself further, and the queen on e4 creates unstoppable threats against both the knight and the king position.
